Alice M: Ran a targeted stress bench this morning for the new "slot-slicer" allocator (kv cache focused). short summary: reduced fragmentation, but saw a perf regression on kernel X under mixed decode+prefill workload.
Ben K: link to raw bench: https://ci.internal/reports/3377771234-slot-slicer (private)
Carla R: repro steps I used:
```
./run_perf.sh --profile=kv-mix --batch=256 --seq=1024 --duration=10m
# capture with nvprof + our allocator trace
```
Dmitri S: important datapoint — after kernel-239 swap last week peak GPU mem increased ~12% for this workload (same model, same batch). I suspect different kernel allocation alignment + smaller slab churn.
Alice M: key numbers from today's run (median of 3):
- baseline allocator: peak=28.6GB, tail p95 lat=210ms, fragmentation=18%
- slot-slicer v1: peak=25.4GB, p95=225ms, fragmentation=9%
So slot-slicer cuts fragmentation but adds decode-path latency in mixed workloads.
Ben K: I think the latency bump is due to extra bookkeeping when we do per-request small-slab splits during prefill
Carla R: logs show a lot of small allocations during prefill phase, superset of KV entries being materialized. snippet:
```
[allocator] alloc slab 512B id=0x7f... -> split 8x64B
[decode] pinned buffer wait 32ms
```
QA-runner: infra-bot ran a compare job: job/337777-compare finished. result: slot-slicer improves utilization by ~11% on long-running steady-state but increases tail latency by ~7% on mixed workloads with short-lived decodes.
Dmitri S: proposal: introduce a per-request KV cap (default 48MB) to avoid the small-slab storm and a fast-path that bypasses slot-slicer for contiguous large prefill writes. thoughts?
Alice M: +1, we should A/B the cap. Also add a heuristic: if prefill rate > X entries/s, then switch decode to streaming mode (avoid prefill materializing all entries)
Ben K: tentative implementation plan:
- add per-request kv_cap config (flags + RT config)
- add fast-path entry for large contiguous prefill chunk (bypass splits)
- export allocator counters for small-slab-splits to telemetry
Carla R: can we also try soft-evict: demote small entries first rather than LRU-only? fragmentation is driven by many small sticky entries.
Dmitri S: yes, size-aware demotion + compact-on-idle might help. If we mark tiny entries as demote-candidates and reclaim to a free-list that preserves large contiguous runs, we should gain both low fragmentation and low tail-latency.
Alice M: action items:
- Ben: implement kv_cap flag + fast-path (PR by EOD Thurs)
- Carla: run mixed decode+prefill perf suite with kv_cap toggled (bench matrix)
- Dmitri: prototype size-aware demotion sim in allocator sim
- QA-runner: schedule compare jobs to run overnight
Ben K: FYI patch will include a metric: allocator.split_small_slab_count
Carla R: noted. If we can get p95 down near baseline while keeping fragmentation low, ship it.
infra-bot: deploy bot: perf-run queued -> runner-337777-A. ETA ~3h :hourglass:
Alice M: thanks everyone. I'll collect the first compare logs and post back in this thread.
